title: Write a broken-link checker for the notes
prompt: Some of the cross-links in my notes have gone stale — files got renamed or moved and the links still point at the old paths. Write tools/check_links.py that checks every markdown file under notes/ (links are relative markdown links resolved against the linking note's folder — see the README) and prints each broken link as `path/to/note.md:LINE -> target`, one per line. Exit code 1 if any links are broken, 0 if the tree is clean. Standard library only, and nothing that touches the network — this machine is offline. Verify with `python3 -m unittest tests.check_n01 -q`.

title: Generate INDEX.md for the whole notes tree
prompt: My notes have outgrown memory. Create INDEX.md at the repo root listing every note under notes/, grouped by folder: one `## <folder>` section per subfolder of notes/ (folder name as the heading, sections alphabetical), and under each section every note in that folder listed exactly once as a relative markdown link, per the linking convention in the README. Verify with `python3 -m unittest tests.check_n02 -q`.

title: Fix the broken cross-links
prompt: A bunch of the cross-links in the notes are broken — targets were renamed or moved and the links were never updated. Find every broken link under notes/ and fix it to point at the right existing note. Update only the link targets: don't rewrite prose, don't add or delete files, don't rename or move anything. Verify with `python3 -m unittest tests.check_n03 -q`.

title: Summarise notes/projects/ into a README
prompt: Write notes/projects/README.md summarising that folder: one `- [title](file.md)` line for each of the other notes in notes/projects/ (a relative markdown link, per the convention in the README), followed by an em-dash and a one-line description of what the note is about. Every note in the folder exactly once, keep it compact. Verify with `python3 -m unittest tests.check_n04 -q`.

title: Build TAGS.md index of inline tags
prompt: I use inline `#tag`s across the notes. Build TAGS.md at the repo root indexing them all: one `## #tag` section per tag (alphabetical), each followed by relative markdown links to every note that uses that tag, per the linking convention in the README. Verify with `python3 -m unittest tests.check_n05 -q`.
